raw_tool_response: User responded: tenant_admin_authority=SUBSEQUENT TENANT ADMIN ASSIGNMENT AND AUTHORITY POLICY  1. AUTHORIZATION AUTHORITY  - Only an authorized Platform Admin may approve subsequent Tenant Admin assignments, removals, and restoration of Tenant Admin privileges. - An existing Tenant Admin may nominate a replacement or submit an administrative change request but must not independently approve or execute the assignment. - Tenant Admin assignment authority must remain separate from ordinary tenant-level role-management permissions. - A Tenant Admin must not grant themselves additional administrative privileges or promote another user to Tenant Admin without explicit Platform Admin authorization.  2. EXECUTION RESPONSIBILITY  - After explicit Platform Admin authorization, the controlled platform provisioning process or an authorized Platform Admin executes the approved change. - The system must verify the target user's identity, tenant membership, account status, and eligibility before applying the assignment. - The approving authority and executing actor/process must be recorded separately. - A requestor must not approve their own request. - Unauthorized, incomplete, or unapproved assignment attempts must be rejected.  3. TENANT ADMIN REMOVAL AND REPLACEMENT  - Removal or revocation of an existing Tenant Admin requires explicit Platform Admin authorization. - The system must prevent removal, disablement, or revocation of the last active Tenant Admin unless an authorized replacement has been successfully assigned or a separately authorized administrative recovery process is available. - Replacement assignment and existing administrator removal must be coordinated to prevent tenant administrative lockout. - All changes must be recorded in the audit history.  4. REACTIVATION AND PRIVILEGE RESTORATION  - Reactivating a previously disabled Tenant Admin account must not automatically restore Tenant Admin privileges. - Restoration of Tenant Admin authority requires a fresh, explicit Platform Admin authorization. - The system must verify current tenant membership, identity, business authorization, and account security before restoring the privilege. - Previous administrative permissions must not be assumed to remain valid merely because the account has been reactivated.  5. SELF-ESCALATION AND SECURITY CONTROLS  - No Tenant Admin may promote themselves or independently authorize another Tenant Admin. - No ordinary user may elevate their own privileges through account recovery, role assignment, or reactivation. - Platform Admin authorization must be explicit, tenant-specific, and auditable. - Platform Admin authority for account administration must not grant tenant-content access or bypass the first-release tenant-content access prohibition. - The last active Platform Admin must also be protected against accidental removal or disablement without an independently authorized recovery process.  6. AUDITABILITY  Record: - Requesting administrator and target user. - Relevant tenant ID. - Requested assignment, removal, or restoration. - Approving Platform Admin identity. - Executing actor or provisioning process. - Authorization decision and business rationale. - Previous and resulting role state. - Effective timestamp and execution outcome.  These rules establish subsequent Tenant Admin authority boundaries for the first release while preserving existing Q2, Q3, and Q4 security and separation-of-duties decisions., bootstrap_recovery_authority=INITIAL PLATFORM ADMIN BOOTSTRAP AND LAST-ADMIN RECOVERY AUTHORITY POLICY  1. INITIAL PLATFORM ADMIN BOOTSTRAP AUTHORIZATION  - The initial Platform Admin must be explicitly authorized by the Organization Owner or a formally designated Security Authority responsible for the SupportIQ platform. - The approval authority must be independent of the person executing the bootstrap operation. - A designated Security / Identity Administrator must verify the nominated individual's identity and eligibility. - An authorized DevOps or Deployment Operator must execute the controlled one-time bootstrap process. - The approving authority, identity verifier, and executing operator must be recorded separately wherever organizational staffing permits. - The initial bootstrap must not depend on an existing Platform Admin, because no Platform Admin exists at this stage. - Public registration, self-registration, or ordinary account recovery must never create the initial Platform Admin. - Bootstrap credentials and temporary privileges must be securely invalidated after successful provisioning.  2. LAST PLATFORM ADMIN RECOVERY  If the last active Platform Admin becomes unavailable, a controlled out-of-band recovery process must be used.  - Recovery must be authorized by the Organization Owner or formally designated Security Authority. - A separate authorized Security / Identity Administrator must independently verify the identity and legitimacy of the recovery request. - An authorized technical operator must execute the approved recovery or replacement procedure. - The requesting individual must not independently approve and execute their own recovery. - A new Platform Admin identity must be explicitly nominated and authorized. - Recovery must not rely on self-registration, ordinary password recovery, or an existing administrator account that is unavailable. - All recovery actions, approvals, identity-verification evidence, and execution outcomes must be recorded in an immutable or tamper-resistant audit trail.  3. LAST TENANT ADMIN RECOVERY  If the last active Tenant Admin becomes unavailable:  - An authorized Platform Admin may approve the appointment of a replacement Tenant Admin for the affected tenant. - An independent authorized technical operator or controlled provisioning process must execute the approved assignment. - The replacement user's identity, account status, and tenant membership must be verified. - The recovery must be limited to restoring tenant administrative control. - It must not grant exceptional Platform Admin access to tenant content. - Existing tenant isolation, role restrictions, and Knowledge Reviewer independence requirements must remain unchanged.  4. INDEPENDENT APPROVAL AND SEPARATION OF DUTIES  - No individual may request, approve, and execute their own privileged bootstrap or last-admin recovery. - Approval, identity verification, and technical execution must be separated between authorized responsibilities. - Where organizational staffing is insufficient to provide three separate individuals, the minimum requirement is independent human authorization and execution, with separate identity-verification evidence and comprehensive audit recording. - No recovery process may be used to bypass existing authorization, self-approval, or tenant-isolation restrictions.  5. IDENTITY VERIFICATION AND RECOVERY SECURITY  - Identity verification must use independently established organizational identity and trusted out-of-band verification channels. - Recovery authorization must include a documented business justification and the identity of the nominated replacement. - Temporary credentials or bootstrap privileges must be securely controlled and invalidated after successful recovery. - Existing sessions and refresh tokens associated with compromised or replaced accounts must be revoked. - Privileged roles must be explicitly assigned after recovery and must not be inherited automatically from previous account states. - MFA and applicable authentication requirements must be enforced before normal administrative access is granted.  6. AUDIT EVIDENCE  The system must record: - Recovery or bootstrap request ID. - Requesting authority and business justification. - Approving Organization Owner / Security Authority. - Independent identity-verification outcome and verifier. - Executing operator or provisioning process. - Nominated and resulting administrator identity. - Relevant tenant ID, where applicable. - Previous and resulting administrative state. - Approval, execution, and completion timestamps. - Session and token revocation outcomes. - Success, failure, and exception details.  Sensitive credentials, passwords, MFA secrets, and recovery codes must never be stored in audit records.  7. PRESERVATION OF EXISTING SECURITY BOUNDARIES  - Account recovery must never grant Platform Admin access to tenant content. - Platform Admin recovery must not bypass the first-release prohibition on exceptional tenant-content access. - Tenant Admin recovery must remain restricted to the affected tenant. - Knowledge Reviewer permissions must require separate explicit authorization. - No recovery process may bypass independent knowledge approval or the prohibition on self-approval. - All recovery and bootstrap operations must preserve least privilege, tenant isolation, and auditability.  These rules define the first-release bootstrap and last-administrator recovery authority. They do not authorize implementation, runtime access, or exceptional tenant-content access., rationale_deferrals=RATIONALE AND EXPLICIT DEFERRALS FOR ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORITY  1. RATIONALE FOR FIRST-RELEASE DECISIONS  The selected authority model is appropriate for the first demonstrable release because it establishes clear administrative accountability, prevents privilege escalation, and avoids dependency on an unavailable administrator.  The model separates authorization, identity verification, and technical execution to ensure that no individual can independently request, approve, and execute their own privileged access.  2. INITIAL PLATFORM ADMIN BOOTSTRAP  The initial Platform Admin must be authorized by the Organization Owner or formally designated Security Authority, independently verified, and provisioned through a controlled one-time bootstrap process executed by an authorized technical operator.  This avoids the circular dependency of requiring an existing Platform Admin when no Platform Admin exists.  3. SUBSEQUENT TENANT ADMIN ASSIGNMENTS  Requiring explicit Platform Admin authorization for subsequent Tenant Admin assignments, removals, and privilege restoration prevents uncontrolled administrative delegation and self-escalation.  Existing Tenant Admins may request or nominate replacements but cannot independently authorize their own privileged administrative succession.  4. LAST-ADMIN RECOVERY  A controlled out-of-band recovery mechanism is necessary to prevent permanent administrative lockout if the last Platform Admin or Tenant Admin becomes unavailable.  Independent authorization, identity verification, controlled execution, and auditable evidence ensure that recovery does not become an alternative privilege-escalation mechanism.  Tenant Admin recovery remains limited to restoring administration of the affected tenant and must not grant Platform Admin access to tenant content.  5. EXPLICIT FIRST-RELEASE SECURITY BOUNDARIES  The first release will enforce:  - Independent authorization for privileged administrator assignments. - Separation of approval, identity verification, and execution. - Prevention of self-authorization and self-escalation. - Protection against accidental removal of the last active administrator. - Explicit authorization before restoring previously disabled privileged roles. - Revocation of affected sessions and tokens during account security recovery. - Strict tenant isolation. - No exceptional Platform Admin tenant-content access or emergency content-access bypass.  6. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED DETAILS  The following operational and implementation details are intentionally deferred:  - Formal organizational designation and delegation procedures for the Organization Owner and Security Authority. - Specific bootstrap deployment tools, infrastructure, and technical execution mechanisms. - Detailed last-administrator recovery runbooks and operational procedures. - Specific identity-verification technologies and evidence formats. - Recovery SLAs, escalation timelines, and notification schedules. - Future automated emergency recovery capabilities.  These deferrals do not create implied authority, permit self-authorization, or weaken any first-release security restriction.  7. OVERALL RATIONALE  The first-release approach prioritizes controlled administration, recoverability, separation of duties, and tenant isolation over administrative convenience.  It provides a sufficiently clear and secure authority model without introducing complex exceptional-access mechanisms before their requirements and security implications have been separately assessed.  All Q2, Q3, and Q4 decisions concerning independent knowledge approval, tenant-scoped permissions, account security, auditability, and the prohibition on exceptional Platform Admin tenant-content access remain unchanged.  These are clarification decisions only and do not constitute PRD modification, Requirement approval, or implementation authorization.
